q: Which of the following BFP-issued documents is required for the building permit?
n: A Fire Safety Evaluation Clearance (FSEC) from the BFP is a prerequisite for the building permit. Source: RA 9514 (Fire Code) 2019 RIRR, Rule 9 (FSEC).

q: Which of the following BFP-issued documents is required for the occupancy permit?
n: A Fire Safety Inspection Certificate (FSIC) from the BFP is required for the certificate of occupancy and for business permits. Source: RA 9514 (Fire Code) 2019 RIRR, Rule 9 (FSIC).

q: A 1.20m diameter circular table can accommodate how many seats?
n: A round table about 1.20 m in diameter seats 4 comfortably, and up to 6 at about 600 mm per person. Source: Panero & Zelnik, Human Dimension and Interior Space (Dining); Neufert, Architects' Data.

q: Which construction system is most suitable for a manufacturing facility requiring fast construction, cost efficiency, and wide clear spans?
n: Pre-engineered buildings (PEB) use factory-made steel frames and cladding that are bolted together quickly. They give wide clear spans at low cost, which suits factories and warehouses. Source: Allen & Iano, Fundamentals of Building Construction, Ch. 11 (Pre-engineered Metal Buildings); MBMA Metal Building Systems Manual.

q: What is the main advantage of a portal frame in low-rise buildings?
n: Portal frames have rigid beam-to-column joints, so they span widely without interior columns. That is the main reason they are used for low-rise sheds and halls. Source: Ching, Building Structures Illustrated (Rigid Frames); Schodek & Bechthold, Structures.

q: What is the connection point called where members meet in a space truss?
n: In a space truss, the members meet at nodes: spherical or plate connectors that join many members. Source: Schodek & Bechthold, Structures (Space Frames); Ching, Building Structures Illustrated.

q: Which document outlines the legal framework, common areas, and management rules for a small residential development or condominium project?
n: The master deed (with its declaration of restrictions) establishes a condominium. It defines the units, the common areas and the management rules. Source: RA 4726 (Condominium Act), Sec. 4; PD 957 IRR.

q: In the computation of plumbing fees, one ____ is composed of 1 WC, 2 FD, 1 LAV, 1 sink, 3 faucets and 1 shower head.
n: For plumbing permit fees, one "unit" is 1 water closet, 2 floor drains, 1 lavatory, 1 sink, 3 faucets and 1 shower head. Source: 2004 Revised IRR of PD 1096 (NBCP), Rule II – Schedule of Fees (Plumbing Permit Fees).

q: What type of Portland Cement is ideal for massive concrete construction?
n: Type IV (low-heat) Portland cement generates the least heat of hydration. That limits thermal cracking in massive pours such as dams and thick foundations. Source: ASTM C150 (Portland Cement Types); Kosmatka et al., Design and Control of Concrete Mixtures (PCA).

q: What concrete class is used for columns and slabs?
n: Structural members such as columns, beams and suspended slabs commonly use Class A concrete (1:2:4, about 21 MPa). Source: Max Fajardo, Simplified Construction Estimate (Concrete Classes); DPWH Standard Specifications, Item 405.

q: A rope used to control a lifted load's swing or rotation during lifting.
n: A tag line is a rope tied to a suspended load. A worker uses it to control swing and rotation during lifting. Source: DOLE OSHS (Construction Safety – Rigging); ASME B30.5 (Mobile Cranes).

q: What shall be the bend diameter if the rebar size is 16mm?
n: Standard hooks on bars from 10 mm through 25 mm need an inside bend diameter of 6 bar diameters. For 16 mm that is 6 × 16 = 96 mm, about 4 in. Source: NSCP 2015, Table 425.3.1 (Minimum Inside Bend Diameters); ACI 318.

q: In pitched-roof construction, what is the horizontal member that connects opposing rafters at their base to prevent them from spreading apart?
n: In pitched roofs, the tie beam (or ceiling joist) joins the feet of opposing rafters. It holds them in tension so they cannot spread. Collar ties sit higher up. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated, Ch. 6 (Rafter Framing).

q: Which of the following is a volume quantity?
n: Building bulk is a volume, the three-dimensional envelope a building may occupy. OFB, development controls and BHL are faces, rules or heights. Source: 2004 Revised IRR of PD 1096 (NBCP), Rule VII (Building Bulk and Building Envelope).

q: Which test is conducted on-site to determine the optimal moisture content and maximum dry density of soil for compaction purposes?
n: The Proctor compaction test finds a soil's optimum moisture content and maximum dry density. That sets the target for field compaction. Source: ASTM D698 / D1557 (Standard and Modified Proctor); Das, Principles of Geotechnical Engineering.

q: What is the primary purpose of using hub and tack in site development?
o: to serve as erosion control points
to indicate precise reference points for layout
n: Hubs (stakes) with tacks driven into their tops mark precise survey reference points for setting out the layout. Source: Brinker & Wolf, Elementary Surveying (Construction Staking); Ching, Building Construction Illustrated, Ch. 1.

q: In a CARI policy, who is theinsurer who assumes the financial risk in case of loss or damage during the construction period?
n: Under a Contractor's All Risk Insurance (CARI) policy, the insurer, the insurance company, assumes the financial risk of loss or damage during construction. Source: Insurance Code of the Philippines (PD 612 as amended by RA 10607); UAP SPP Doc. 301 (Insurance).

q: What is the main basis for determining payment amounts in a construction progress billing?
n: Progress billings are based on the schedule of values, which breaks the contract sum into work items. Payment is based on the percentage completed on each item. Source: AIA G702/G703 (Application and Certificate for Payment); UAP SPP Doc. 301.

q: Which of the following is an example of a floating floor system that uses interlocking edges for installation without adhesive or mechanical fasteners?
n: Click-lock flooring (laminate, engineered or vinyl) has interlocking edges that snap together. It floats on the underlay without glue or nails. Source: NWFA Installation Guidelines (Floating Floors); manufacturers' installation guides.

q: Which type of tile features patterns made by inlaid colors rather than surface glaze?
n: Encaustic tiles get their pattern from colored clays inlaid into the body, not from a surface glaze. The pattern lasts as the tile wears. Source: Harris, Dictionary of Architecture and Construction (Encaustic Tile); TCNA Handbook.

q: Why was popcorn ceiling originally used in residential construction?
o: to hide imperfections and absorb sound
to make ceilings easier to clean
n: Popcorn (acoustic) ceiling texture was sprayed on to hide surface defects cheaply and to absorb some sound. Source: Harris, Dictionary of Architecture and Construction (Acoustic Ceiling Texture); US EPA (asbestos-era popcorn ceilings).

q: Which of the following spaces typically requires the use of cement backer board behind wall tiles?
n: Shower areas need cement backer board behind the tiles. Unlike gypsum board, it does not deteriorate when wet. Source: TCNA Handbook (Wet Area Installations); ANSI A118.9 (Cementitious Backer Units).

q: What is a key benefit of passive design?
n: Passive design uses orientation, shading, daylighting and natural ventilation to cut the need for mechanical cooling and lighting. The result is lower energy use. Source: Lechner, Heating, Cooling, Lighting; Philippine Green Building Code (2015).

q: Which is a sustainable material choice for green buildings?
n: Bamboo grows quickly, renews itself and stores carbon, so it is a sustainable material. PVC, imported granite and some laminates have high embodied impacts. Source: Philippine Green Building Code (2015), Materials; ISO 22156 (Bamboo Structures).

q: Which of the following refers to custom-fabricated wood components like moldings, trims, stair parts, and paneling installed in interior spaces?
n: Millwork is custom-fabricated wood such as moldings, trims, stair parts and paneling, produced in a mill and installed on site. Source: Architectural Woodwork Standards (AWI); Harris, Dictionary of Architecture and Construction.

q: In a kitchen renovation project, which term best describes pre-fabricated modular storage units like base and wall cabinets?
n: Casework is prefabricated modular cabinetry: base cabinets, wall cabinets and storage units. Source: Architectural Woodwork Standards (AWI, Casework); CSI MasterFormat Division 12.

q: Which certification should you check when selecting carpets for improved indoor air quality in residential or commercial interiors?
n: The Carpet and Rug Institute's Green Label (Plus) certifies carpets and adhesives with low VOC emissions for better indoor air quality. Source: Carpet and Rug Institute (CRI) Green Label Plus program; LEED v4 EQ Low-Emitting Materials.

q: What is the ideal use of beadboard in interior applications?
n: Beadboard, narrow boards with a bead along each joint, is mainly used as decorative wainscoting on lower walls and as ceiling cladding. Source: Harris, Dictionary of Architecture and Construction; Ching, Interior Design Illustrated.

q: Which method is commonly used in site development to achieve instant ground cover and minimize soil erosion on exposed slopes?
n: Sodding lays pre-grown turf, which covers the ground instantly and protects slopes from erosion at once. Seeding and hydroseeding need time to establish. Source: De Chiara & Koppelman, Time-Saver Standards for Site Planning (Erosion Control); US EPA, Erosion and Sediment Control.

q: Which concept in urban design is Ian Bentley best known for contributing to?
n: Ian Bentley is the lead author of Responsive Environments: A Manual for Designers (1985). It sets out principles such as permeability, variety, legibility and robustness. Source: Bentley et al., Responsive Environments (1985).

q: According to Ian Bentley’s urban design principles, which concept refers to the ability of a space to accommodate a variety of uses over time?
n: In Responsive Environments, robustness is a place's ability to accommodate different uses over time. Source: Bentley et al., Responsive Environments (1985).

q: Combination of paved unroofed open spaces and the building footprint.
n: The construction area is the building footprint plus the paved, unroofed (impervious) areas, that is PSO + ISA. Its maximum is MACA. Source: 2004 Revised IRR of PD 1096 (NBCP), Rule VIII, Table VIII.1 (note c).

q: Minimum clear width of Group A dwelling stairs.
n: Stairs in Group A dwellings must have a clear width of at least 750 mm. Source: 2004 Revised IRR of PD 1096 (NBCP), Rule VII, Sec. 708 (Minimum Requirements for Group A Dwellings – Stairs).

q: Maximum rise height according to the RA 9514.
n: The Fire Code limits riser height to 180 mm, with a minimum tread of 280 mm. Source: RA 9514 (Fire Code) 2019 RIRR, Div. 10.2.5 (Stairs).

q: What is required if a staircase exceeds 2.24 m in width?
n: Stairs wider than about 2.24 m need intermediate handrails, so every part of the width is within reach of a rail. Source: NFPA 101, Sec. 7.2.2.4.1.2; RA 9514 (Fire Code) 2019 RIRR.

q: For a commercial building, what is the maximum distance of the off-site parking provisions?
n: Off-site parking for a commercial building must be within 200 m of the building it serves. Source: 2004 Revised IRR of PD 1096 (NBCP), Rule VII, Sec. 707 (Parking – off-site provisions).

q: In building height computation, EGL means what?
n: EGL means Established Grade Line, the reference elevation from which building height is measured. Source: 2004 Revised IRR of PD 1096 (NBCP), Rule VII (Building Height Limit).

q: Which government agency in the Philippines is responsible for mapping, surveying, and providing geospatial data?
n: NAMRIA (National Mapping and Resource Information Authority) is the national agency for mapping, surveying and geospatial data. Source: Executive Order No. 192 (1987), creation of NAMRIA under the DENR.
